title: API Overview
content:
The CodeMirror component has three kinds of API:

Page	Content
Props	Options that configure the editor. Changes are applied without recreating it.
Events	Notifications for loading, focus, document changes, and destruction.
Instance API	Properties and methods available through a template ref.

<script setup lang="ts">




const value = ref('');
const cm = ref<CodeMirrorExposed>();
</script>

<template>
  <code-mirror
    ref="cm"
    v-model="value"
    basic
    :lang="javascript()"
    @ready="() => cm?.view?.focus()"
  />
</template>

title: Instance API
content:
Access the instance through a template ref. Use the CodeMirrorExposed type for type checking.

<script setup lang="ts">



const cm = ref<CodeMirrorExposed>();

const insertDate = () => {
  cm.value?.replaceSelection(new Date().toISOString());
};
</script>

<template>
  <code-mirror ref="cm" basic />
  <button type="button" @click="insertDate">Insert date</button>
</template>

The editor is created after mount. Until the ready event, view and the values derived from it are undefined or empty.

Properties

Property	Type	Description
view	EditorView | undefined	The EditorView. Use it for anything not wrapped by the component.
editor	HTMLElement | undefined	The root element that contains the editor.
dom	Element | undefined	The editable content element.
selection	EditorSelection | undefined	Gets or sets the selection.
cursor	number	Gets or sets the cursor position.
focus	boolean	Gets or sets the focus state.
length	number	Length of the document.
json	Record<string, StateField<unknown>>	Gets or sets the state as a JSON-serializable object.
diagnosticCount	number	Number of lint diagnostics. See diagnosticCount.

Methods

Method	Description
lint()	Runs the linter immediately. Only works when the linter prop is set.
forceReconfigure()	Removes and re-registers all extensions.

CodeMirror 5 compatible methods

These methods are provided for users familiar with CodeMirror 5. The properties above and view are usually sufficient, so active use is not recommended.

Method	Description
getRange(from?: number, to?: number)	Gets the text between the given positions.
getLine(number: number)	Gets the content of a line.
lineCount()	Gets the number of lines.
getCursor()	Gets one end of the primary selection.
listSelections()	Gets all current selection ranges.
getSelection()	Gets the selected text.
getSelections()	Gets the text of every selection range.
somethingSelected()	Returns true if any text is selected.
replaceRange(replacement: string | Text, from, to)	Replaces the text between from and to.
replaceSelection(replacement: string | Text)	Replaces the selection(s).
setCursor(position: number)	Sets the cursor position.
setSelection(anchor: number, head?: number)	Sets a single selection range.
setSelections(ranges: readonly SelectionRange[], primary?: number)	Sets multiple selection ranges.
extendSelectionsBy(f: (range: SelectionRange) => number)	Extends every selection by the result of f.

title: Props
content:
Props are written in kebab-case in templates (tab-size) and camelCase in JavaScript (tabSize).

Content

Prop	Type	Default	Description
model-value	string | Text	''	The document. Use with v-model. (Not value.)
placeholder	string | HTMLElement	undefined	Shown while the document is empty. See placeholder.
tag	string	'div'	Tag name of the root element.

Setup

Prop	Type	Default	Description
basic	boolean	false	Enables basicSetup.
minimal	boolean	false	Enables minimalSetup. basic takes precedence.

Editing

Prop	Type	Default	Description
readonly	boolean	false	Prevents changes but keeps the editor focusable. See readOnly.
disabled	boolean	false	Makes the editor non-editable and non-focusable. Inverse of editable.
wrap	boolean	false	Enables line wrapping.
tab	boolean	false	Indents with the Tab key (indentWithTab).
tab-size	number	undefined	Tab size.
indent-unit	string	undefined	Indentation unit.
allow-multiple-selections	boolean	false	Allows multiple selections.
line-separator	string	undefined	Line separator. \n when not set.
keymap	KeyBinding[]	[]	Custom key bindings.

Language and linting

Prop	Type	Default	Description
lang	LanguageSupport	undefined	Language for syntax highlighting. See languages.
linter	LintSource	undefined	Lint source, e.g. jsonParseLinter() or esLint(...).
linter-config	object	{}	Linter config.
force-linting	boolean	false	Runs the linter right away. See forceLinting.
gutter	boolean	false	Shows the lint gutter. Requires linter.
gutter-config	object	undefined	Lint gutter config.

Appearance

Prop	Type	Default	Description
dark	boolean	false	Marks the editor theme as dark.
theme	Record<string, StyleSpec>	{}	Style spec passed to EditorView.theme.
phrases	Record<string, string>	undefined	UI translations.

Scrolling

Prop	Type	Default	Description
scroll-into-view	boolean	true	Scrolls to the selection when modelValue is updated externally. See scrollIntoView.
preserve-scroll-position	boolean	false	Keeps the scroll position when modelValue is updated externally. See scrollSnapshot.

Extensions

Prop	Type	Default	Description
extensions	Extension[]	[]	Additional extensions, appended after the ones generated from props.

title: Getting Started
content:
Installation

Install the component together with codemirror:

pnpm add vue-codemirror6 codemirror

Language support, linters, and themes are separate packages. Install the ones you need, for example:

pnpm add @codemirror/lang-javascript

Minimal example

<script setup lang="ts">



const value = ref('Cozy lummox gives smart squid who asks for job pen.');
</script>

<template>
  <code-mirror v-model="value" />
</template>

This renders a plain editor without line numbers or key bindings. Add the basic prop to enable CodeMirror's basicSetup (line numbers, history, bracket matching, search, and more):

<template>
  <code-mirror v-model="value" basic />
</template>

Use minimal instead of basic for minimalSetup. If both are set, basic takes precedence.

Adding a language

Pass a LanguageSupport object to the lang prop to enable syntax highlighting:

<script setup lang="ts">




const value = ref('console.log("Hello, World!");');
const lang = javascript();
</script>

<template>
  <code-mirror v-model="value" basic :lang="lang" />
</template>

Global registration

The package exports an install function that registers the component as CodeMirror:

createApp(App).use(CodeMirror).mount('#app');

After that, <code-mirror> can be used in any template without importing it.

Package exports

Export	Description
default	The Vue component.
install	Vue plugin function that registers the component globally.
CodeMirror	The component wrapped with defineCustomElement.
CodeMirrorExposed	Type of the instance API exposed through a template ref.
Meta	Package version and build date.
vue-codemirror6/umd	UMD build for loading with a <script> tag.

Next steps

Usage — v-model, slots, read-only mode, and key bindings.

Languages, Linters & Themes

title: Introduction
content:
vue-codemirror6 is a component for using CodeMirror 6 in Vue. It is built on vue-demi, so the same component works in both Vue 2.7 and Vue 3.

CodeMirror 6 is a modular code editor. Instead of exposing every CodeMirror concept directly, this component turns the most common settings into props and keeps the rest available through extensions and the editor instance.

Features

v-model binding for the document text.

Common settings as props: basic / minimal setup, line wrapping, tab indentation, read-only and disabled modes, placeholder, dark mode, and more.

Language, linter, and theme props that accept any CodeMirror package.

Events for ready, focus, update, change, and destroy.

Instance API to access the EditorView, selection, cursor, lint diagnostics, and CodeMirror 5 style helpers.

SSR compatibility: the editor is only created on the client.

Web Component build of the same component (experimental).

Supported environments

Environment	Version
Vue	^2.7.14 or ^3.3.4
CodeMirror	codemirror ^6.0.0
Output	ESM (default) and UMD build

The @codemirror/* packages (state, view, language, lint, commands, autocomplete, search) are peer dependencies. They are installed together with the codemirror package.

Next steps

Getting Started — install the package and render your first editor.

Playground — try the live demo.

Props — the full list of options.

title: Languages, Linters & Themes
content:
Languages

Install a language package and pass its LanguageSupport object to lang:

<script setup lang="ts">



const lang = markdown();
</script>

<template>
  <code-mirror basic wrap :lang="lang" />
</template>

Official language packages include:

@codemirror/lang-angular, lang-cpp, lang-css, lang-html, lang-java, lang-javascript, lang-json, lang-lezer, lang-markdown, lang-php, lang-python, lang-rust, lang-sql, lang-vue, lang-wast, lang-xml

Many community packages are also available. See the CodeMirror language list and the list below.

@phoenix-plugin-registry/petetnt.brackets-codemirror-fortran

@phoenix-plugin-registry/petetnt.brackets-codemirror-go

@acarl005/lang-sql

@ark-us/codemirror-lang-taylor

@formulavize/lang-fiz

@gravitywiz/codemirror-lang-gfcalc

@nextjournal/lang-clojure

@plutojl/lang-julia

@polybase/codemirror-lang-javascript

@replit/codemirror-lang-nix

@replit/codemirror-lang-csharp

@replit/codemirror-lang-solidity

@replit/codemirror-lang-svelte

@zhijiu/lang-sql

codemirror-lang-bool

codemirror-lang-brainfuck

codemirror-lang-cherry

codemirror-lang-chordpro

codemirror-lang-circom

codemirror-lang-edn

codemirror-lang-statement

gcode-lang-codemirror

gmail-lang

lang-bqn

lang-clojure

lang-d

lang-feel

lang-firestore

Linters

Pass a LintSource to linter. Add gutter to show a marker on lines with problems.

<script setup lang="ts">




const value = ref('{ "key": "value", }');
</script>

<template>
  <code-mirror v-model="value" basic gutter :lang="json()" :linter="jsonParseLinter()" />
</template>

For JavaScript, @codemirror/lang-javascript provides esLint(), which can be combined with eslint-linter-browserify:

const linter = esLint(new eslint.Linter(), {
  languageOptions: {
    parserOptions: { ecmaVersion: 2022, sourceType: 'module' }
  },
  rules: { semi: ['error', 'never'] }
});

Prop	Description
linter	The lint source.
linter-config	Linter configuration such as delay.
force-linting	Runs the linter immediately instead of waiting for the editor to become idle.
gutter	Shows the lint gutter. Has no effect without linter.
gutter-config	Lint gutter configuration.

The number of diagnostics is available as diagnosticCount on the instance, and lint() runs the linter on demand.

In the editor, Ctrl+Shift+M (Cmd+Shift+M on macOS) opens the lint panel and F8 jumps to the next diagnostic.

Themes and dark mode

dark tells CodeMirror that the editor has a dark background, so built-in UI such as the selection and panels use dark colors.

theme accepts a style spec object passed to EditorView.theme.

<script setup lang="ts">


const theme = {
  '&': { fontSize: '14px' },
  '.cm-content': { fontFamily: 'Menlo, monospace' },
  '.cm-gutters': { backgroundColor: 'transparent', border: 'none' }
};
</script>

<template>
  <code-mirror basic :dark="isDark" :theme="theme" />
</template>

Ready-made themes are usually distributed as extensions. Add them through extensions:

<script setup lang="ts">


</script>

<template>
  <code-mirror basic dark :extensions="[oneDark]" />
</template>

Examples: @codemirror/theme-one-dark, @uiw/codemirror-themes, codemirror6-bootstrap-theme.

Other extensions

Any CodeMirror Extension can be passed through extensions. They are combined with the extensions generated from the other props.

<script setup lang="ts">



const extensions = [EditorView.contentAttributes.of({ spellcheck: 'true' })];
</script>

<template>
  <code-mirror basic :extensions="extensions" />
</template>

lang and linter could also be passed through extensions. They are separate props for type safety and for compatibility with earlier versions.

When props change, the component reconfigures the editor automatically. If you change something the component cannot detect, call forceReconfigure() on the instance.

title: Server-Side Rendering
content:
The component is SSR compatible. CodeMirror is only created in the browser (in onMounted), so during server rendering the component outputs its empty container element without touching window or document.

Nuxt 3 / Nuxt 4

Use the component directly:

<script setup lang="ts">




const value = ref('console.log("Hello, World!");');
const lang = javascript();
</script>

<template>
  <code-mirror v-model="value" basic :lang="lang" />
</template>

Nuxt 2 or when problems occur

Wrap the component with <ClientOnly> so that it is rendered only in the browser:

<template>
  <client-only>
    <code-mirror v-model="value" basic :lang="lang" />
  </client-only>
</template>

Because the editor is created after hydration, the instance properties (view, selection, …) are undefined on the server and until the ready event is emitted on the client.

title: Usage
content:
Two-way binding with v-model The document is bound through modelValue (not value), so v-model works as with any Vue component. When modelValue is changed from outside, the editor content is replaced. Two props control how the view behaves at that moment: scroll-into-view (default true) scrolls the editor to the updated selection. preserve-scroll-position (default false) keeps the current scroll position, which is useful when text is appended continuously (logs, streaming output, and so on). Initial text from a slot Instead of v-model, you can place the initial text inside the component. Only the text of the first child node is used. Slot content overwrites the v-model value, so do not combine the two. The slot method is intended for simple read-only highlighting. Wrap the text in 
 so that whitespace is not collapsed.

The slot method does not work with Vue 2.7.

Read-only and disabled

Prop	Editable	Focusable / selectable	CodeMirror option
readonly	No	Yes	EditorState.readOnly
disabled	No	No	Inverse of EditorView.editable

Use disabled when the editor is only a syntax highlighter.



Editing behavior

Prop	Effect
wrap	Enables line wrapping.
tab	Indents with the Tab key instead of moving focus.
tab-size	Width of a tab character.
indent-unit	Indentation unit, for example "  " or "\t".
allow-multiple-selections	Allows multiple selections (e.g. with Ctrl/Cmd + click).
line-separator	Line separator used for the document. Defaults to \n.
placeholder	Text or an HTMLElement shown while the document is empty.

The tab prop traps the Tab key inside the editor. Keyboard users can still leave the editor by pressing Escape followed by Tab.

Custom key bindings

Pass an array of KeyBinding objects to keymap. If run returns true, the default behavior for that key is skipped.





Listening to events



See Events for the payload of each event.

Translating the editor UI

Use phrases to translate the text shown by CodeMirror (search panel, lint panel, folding markers, …). See the CodeMirror translation example for the available keys.





When combining with vue-i18n, make phrases reactive (for example a computed) so the editor updates when the locale changes. See Internationalization for a full translation table and a vue-i18n example.
